title: Community Rule (1QS) — Hobah Translation
about: The Community Rule, conventionally designated 1QS or Serekh ha-Yahad, is one of the foundational sectarian manuscripts from Qumran Cave 1. It describes entrance into the covenant community, annual covenant ceremony, the doctrine of the two spirits, communal order, discipline, leadership, and hymnic reflection. Parallel and variant Rule manuscripts survive from Cave 4, so 1QS is a major recension, not the only form of the Rule tradition.

translation.status: Hobah provisional source-language reading translation of the substantially preserved 1QS columns
translation.base_text: The Hebrew manuscript 1QS from Qumran Cave 1, following the standard column divisions and the broadly established consonantal readings of the manuscript tradition
translation.method: Fresh modern-English reading translation from the Hebrew sense. No modern copyrighted English translation is copied. Brackets and ellipses signal damaged, restored, or omitted uncertain wording; sectarian terms such as Yahad are rendered contextually as 'Community' while key meanings are disclosed in notes.
translation.confidence: Medium-high in well-preserved columns; medium or lower where the manuscript is damaged or readings/restorations are disputed
translation.notes: This is a reading edition rather than a diplomatic transcription. It covers the substantially preserved content of 1QS by column, while refusing to invent wording where the manuscript is defective. Cave 4 variants are not silently merged into 1QS.
translation.license_note: The underlying Hebrew manuscript is an ancient public-domain text. Hobah English wording is newly prepared for this project.

chapters.label: Column I — Purpose and covenant
chapters.text: [The Instructor shall teach] all the sons of light about the nature of every human being, according to every kind of spirit allotted to them, the signs of their deeds through their generations, and the visitation of their punishments together with the times of their peace. The members of the Community shall seek God with all the heart and all the soul, doing what is good and upright before him as he commanded through Moses and through all his servants the prophets. They shall love everything he chose and hate everything he rejected; they shall distance themselves from every evil thing, cling to every good work, practice truth, righteousness, and justice in the land, and no longer walk in the stubbornness of a guilty heart. All who freely devote themselves to God's truth shall bring their knowledge, strength, and possessions into the Community of God, to purify their knowledge in the truth of his statutes and to distribute their strength according to the perfection of his ways. When they enter the covenant, the priests shall recount God's righteous acts, the Levites shall recount the iniquities of the sons of Israel, and those entering shall confess: ‘We have acted perversely; we and our fathers before us have sinned and rebelled.’

chapters.label: Column II — Blessing, curse, and ordered covenant
chapters.text: The priests shall bless all those who belong to God's lot, saying: ‘May he bless you with every good thing and guard you from every evil. May he illuminate your heart with life-giving understanding and grant you eternal knowledge. May he lift up his gracious face toward you for everlasting peace.’ The Levites shall curse all who belong to the lot of Belial, and the covenant members shall answer, ‘Amen, amen.’ They shall also pronounce a curse on anyone who enters the covenant while secretly setting up the stumbling block of his own heart, intending to turn back and follow it. Such a man shall not say, ‘I will have peace though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart,’ for the curses of this covenant will cling to him. Year by year the covenant shall be renewed. Priests shall pass first according to their spirits, Levites second, and all the people after them in their thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, each person knowing his standing within the Community. No one shall move down from his assigned place or rise above his appointed rank without the judgment of the community.

chapters.label: Column III — Purification and the two spirits
chapters.text: No one is made clean merely by entering water while refusing God's statutes. The unrepentant cannot be sanctified by seas and rivers, purified by ritual washings, or made acceptable by offerings while they despise the judgments of God. A person is purified from wickedness through a humble spirit, by submitting the soul to all God's commands; then the flesh may be cleansed by sprinkling waters and sanctified by waters of purification. The Instructor shall explain that the God of knowledge established all that is and all that will be. Before beings existed he determined their purposes, and when they come into existence they fulfill their appointed work. He created humanity to rule the world and placed within humankind two spirits in which to walk until the appointed visitation: the spirits of truth and perversity. The origin of truth is in a fountain of light; the origin of perversity is in a source of darkness. The Prince of Lights rules over all the sons of righteousness, while the Angel of Darkness rules over the sons of perversity. Yet the God of Israel and his angel of truth assist all the sons of light.

chapters.label: Column IV — Ways and destinies of truth and perversity
chapters.text: These are the ways of the spirit of truth in the world: humility, patience, abundant mercy, enduring goodness, understanding, wisdom, zealous devotion to righteous ordinances, holy purpose with steadfast inclination, great love for all the sons of truth, reverent purity that hates every unclean idol, modest conduct with discernment in every matter, and concealment of the truth's mysteries where they must be guarded. The reward of those who walk in this spirit is healing, abundant peace in length of days, fruitful descendants with every lasting blessing, eternal joy in unending life, and a crown of glory with a garment of majesty in everlasting light. The ways of the spirit of perversity are greed, slackness in righteousness, wickedness and falsehood, pride and haughtiness, deceit and cruelty, impatience, much folly, arrogant zeal, works of abomination, impurity, a blaspheming tongue, blindness of eyes and dullness of ears. Its visitation is destruction without remnant in the dark fire. God permits the two spirits to contend until the appointed time; afterward he will destroy perversity and purify human beings by the spirit of truth, cleansing every deed of wickedness.

chapters.label: Column V — Admission and separation from injustice
chapters.text: This is the rule for the members of the Community who freely turn from every evil and hold fast to everything God commanded. They shall separate from the company of the men of injustice and become one Community in Torah and possessions, answering to the sons of Zadok, the priests who keep the covenant, and to the multitude of the Community who hold fast to it. Every decision concerning law, property, and judgment shall be made according to them. Whoever enters shall swear to return to the Torah of Moses with all his heart and soul, according to everything revealed from it to the sons of Zadok and to the men of their covenant. He shall separate from the men of perversity and shall not mingle his property with theirs, receive from them without proper exchange, or rely upon them in matters of law and judgment. The members shall rebuke one another truthfully, humbly, and lovingly. No one shall speak to his brother in anger or with a stiff neck, nor hate him in a concealed heart; on the same day he shall bring reproof, and he shall not incur guilt because of him.

chapters.label: Column VI — Assembly, meals, and probation
chapters.text: Wherever ten members of the Community are found, a priest shall not be absent among them. Each shall sit before the others according to his rank, and in that order they shall ask counsel in every matter. When they prepare the table for eating or the wine for drinking, the priest shall first stretch out his hand to bless the first portion of bread and wine. An Instructor shall be present among the ten continually, and they shall keep watch together for a third of every night during the year, reading the book, studying the law, and blessing together. A person seeking admission shall first be examined concerning his understanding and deeds. If he is fit, he shall enter the covenant but shall not touch the pure meal of the Many. After a first period of testing he may approach more closely, yet his property remains separately recorded. After a further year, if the Many judge his conduct and understanding suitable, his property is merged with the Community and he may share fully in its sacred food. His rank is thereafter determined in the annual examination along with all the members.

chapters.label: Column VII — Discipline within the Community
chapters.text: A member who knowingly lies about property shall be excluded from the pure meal and shall lose a portion of his food for a set time. One who answers his companion stubbornly, speaks impatiently, or disregards the authority of a brother properly ranked before him shall undergo discipline. Whoever pronounces the divine Name frivolously or uses speech that dishonours what is holy faces severe exclusion. Slander, unjust anger, deliberate deception, insulting a companion, foolish laughter, indecent exposure, spitting in the midst of an assembly, and other violations of communal dignity receive specified penalties according to their seriousness. A person who deserts the Community after many years and then returns is not restored casually; his case must be judged, his former share is not automatically recovered, and repeated abandonment can lead to permanent exclusion. No member may overturn the community's discipline by privately supporting one who has been expelled. The purpose of correction is that the Community remain ordered in truth, humility, justice, love, and reverence rather than becoming a gathering ruled by appetite or anger.

chapters.label: Column VIII — The council and the way in the wilderness
chapters.text: In the council of the Community there shall be twelve men and three priests, perfected in everything revealed from the whole Torah, practicing truth, righteousness, justice, steadfast love, and humble conduct. They shall preserve faith in the land with firm purpose and broken spirit, making atonement for iniquity through works of justice and through suffering under judgment. When these are established in Israel, the council of the Community shall be founded in truth as an everlasting planting, a holy house for Israel and a foundation of the holy of holies for Aaron, true witnesses for judgment and chosen by favour to make atonement for the land. They shall be a tested wall and a precious cornerstone whose foundations will not shake. When such men exist, they shall separate from the dwelling of the men of injustice and go into the wilderness to prepare there the way of the Lord, as it is written: ‘In the wilderness prepare the way of the Lord; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.’ This way is the study of the Torah which he commanded through Moses, so that they may do according to everything revealed in its appointed time.

chapters.label: Column IX — Counsel, law, and expectation
chapters.text: The Community shall be a holy house for Aaron, joined together as a most holy council, and a house of Community for Israel who walk blamelessly. They shall atone for guilt by practicing justice and offering the obedience of the lips rather than the flesh of burnt offerings when proper sacrifice is not available. No one shall knowingly depart from any command. A member who reveals a hidden matter entrusted to the Community or who acts treacherously against its counsel shall be judged according to the seriousness of the offence. The wise shall conceal what should be concealed and reveal what should be revealed. They shall distinguish between righteous and wicked, measure each person according to his spirit, and love or reject deeds according to God's judgment rather than personal impulse. The community's interpreter of the law shall continually study what is hidden in the Torah. The members shall be ruled by the first ordinances in which they began to be instructed until the coming of the prophet and the anointed ones of Aaron and Israel. Until that appointed time, their life is to be governed by disciplined counsel, truthful judgment, and careful interpretation.

chapters.label: Column X — A rule of continual praise
chapters.text: The wise person shall bless the Creator at every appointed time. At the beginning of the rule of light and when it turns toward its appointed dwelling; at the beginning of the watches of darkness and when morning returns; at the appointed times of days and months, at the turning of seasons and years, and at the beginnings of their fixed periods, he shall recount God's righteousness. When he stretches out his hand and when he draws it back, when he goes out and when he comes in, when he sits and when he rises, when he lies upon his bed, he shall praise him. He will not repay evil to anyone with evil. He will pursue a person with goodness, for judgment of every living thing belongs to God, and God himself will repay. He will not envy with a spirit of wickedness, nor desire wealth gained by violence. His zeal shall be for the law of righteousness. He will not contend with the men of destruction until the day of vengeance, but he will not turn away from God's statutes because of fear, threat, or the approval of human beings.

chapters.label: Column XI — Hymn of dependence on God
chapters.text: As for me, my justification belongs to God. In his hand is the perfection of my way and the uprightness of my heart. By his righteous acts he wipes away my transgression. From the source of his knowledge he has opened light for me, and my eye has looked upon his wonders and the light of my heart upon the mystery that is to come. The Being who endures is the support of my right hand; the way of my steps is upon strong rock which no force can shake. For the truth of God is the rock of my steps, and his strength supports my right hand. From the fountain of his righteousness comes my judgment, and from his wonderful mysteries comes the light in my heart. What is a human being among your wondrous works? One born of woman—what is he among your fearsome deeds? He is formed from dust, kneaded with water; guilt and sin are his foundation, impurity and shameful nakedness. Yet by your goodness alone a person is made righteous, and by the abundance of your mercies you cause him to stand before you forever.
